moduleTitle: Lesson 6 - Install and Use Custom Controls
learningObjectives: Explain what a custom control is and what problem it solves.
Describe how a custom control changes the way Tosca sees a complex widget.
Know where custom controls come from and how they are made available to Tosca.
Evaluate supported TBox steering, workarounds, compatible adapters and Vision AI for the actual control.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: The problem: widgets that aren't standard controls

elements.term: When an engine sees the wrong thing
elements.description: Standard identification works because the engine recognises a control as something it understands — a text box, a checkbox, a table. Complex or third-party UI widgets break that assumption. A custom date picker, a rich grid, or a bespoke component may be built from dozens of nested primitive elements, so the engine sees a pile of divs or panels rather than one meaningful control. You can sometimes still automate it, but the steering is fragile and the Module is unreadable.

The original AE1 exercise demonstrates DLL extensions for two controls that standard TBox scanning does not correctly expose: a customized combo box and a table built from DIV elements. With the supplied compatible extensions, these can be scanned and steered as a combo box and table. This result is specific to the exercise controls, not a guarantee for every widget or ActionMode.

elements.text: Adapting a widget can preserve the familiar TestStep workflow. It does not guarantee support for all ActionModes, nor immunity to changes in the application.

bulletPoints: Custom DLL adapters can refine recognition; check product and widget compatibility.
The familiar Module/TestStep workflow can remain applicable; recognition and supported actions still require validation.

elements.description: AE1 Lesson 06 supplies FancyComboBox.dll and HtmlTable.dll as separate attachments. A compiled extension is distinct from a scanned Module or a TestCase object. Obtain the extension and deployment instructions for the actual product and version; the exercise does not teach DLL development inside Commander.

elements.term: On-prem deployment in the original exercise
elements.description: The Tosca 16.0 Academy exercise closes Tosca, places the extracted DLL files in C:\Program Files (x86)\TRICENTIS\Tosca Testsuite\TBox, and reopens Commander before rescanning. This is the documented training-installation path, not a universal path for other installations or future versions. Confirm the installed product’s extension instructions.

elements.text: Validate the extension’s product/version compatibility and deployment on execution environments. Checking test objects into a repository is not evidence that their external dependencies are available on every agent.

Tosca Cloud uses a different route: an administrator uploads via Configurations → Uploads → Custom controls and Launcher distributes the files. That procedure does not affect on-prem customizations and is not the AE1 installation exercise.

bulletPoints: The original exercise supplies two DLLs: FancyComboBox.dll and HtmlTable.dll.
Its on-prem sequence is close Tosca, copy extracted DLLs to the training TBox directory, reopen Commander and rescan. Do not substitute Cloud distribution.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Using them and where they fit

elements.description: With a compatible adapter, scan and check the recognized control and supported operations. Continue through the ordinary Module/TestStep workflow only after confirming that the adapter supports the required actions.

elements.title: An independent troubleshooting sequence
items: 1. Check supported technology and identification properties, anchors or index.
2. Evaluate an alternative supported engine where appropriate.
3. Investigate a compatible widget adapter with its applicable deployment instructions.
4. Evaluate image recognition when structural identification is unavailable, and validate its environmental sensitivity.

elements.text: Structural adaptation can reduce reliance on appearance, but its resilience depends on the widget and adapter. The sequence above is independent guidance, not a verified Academy rule or guarantee that any cosmetic change is safe.

The exercise suggests customizations when supported TBox steering or a workaround cannot handle a control. It also suggests considering Vision AI as a possible alternative to custom development. Neither the exercise nor the independent troubleshooting outline guarantees recognition for every target.

elements.title: Original AE1 exercise, summarized
items: Use the course’s Custom Controls Modules area and open the customized combo-box obstacle (66744). Scan it and create a TestCase to observe the original steering problem.
Open the DIV-table obstacle (57445) and inspect why the initial scan does not expose it as a table.
Use the two official lesson DLL attachments and the documented Tosca 16.0 close/copy/reopen sequence above.
Rescan the combo box after reopening Commander and save the new recognition in a Module.
Create the Fancy Combo Box TestCase in the course’s Custom Controls TestCases area. Add the scanned Module, choose Planned as the value and Input as the ActionMode.
Mark the training TestCase Completed and execute it in ScratchBook. Repeat scanning and steering validation for the DIV table.

bulletPoints: Validate recognition and supported operations after deployment.
Compare supported structural and visual approaches for the actual widget; neither guarantees universal reliability.

examPitfalls.title: Expecting to create custom controls inside Tosca Commander
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Looking for a 'Create Custom Control' option in the Modules section.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: The exercise supplies compiled DLL attachments. Scanning a Module does not create that compiled extension; DLL development is separate from authoring ordinary Commander test objects.

examPitfalls.title: Treating a custom control as a project-level change
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Installing the DLL locally, checking the working TestCases into the common repository, and assuming colleagues and execution agents will be fine.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Confirm compatible external dependencies on execution environments. Repository check-in does not by itself deploy or validate an extension package.

examPitfalls.title: Treating a troubleshooting order as a mandatory engine rule
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming every unsupported widget must use a custom DLL before any visual approach can be considered.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Evaluate the actual supported TBox behavior and workarounds. The Academy exercise also identifies Vision AI as a possible way to avoid customization. Choose and validate an appropriate approach for the target; no universal sequence or immunity to UI changes is promised.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming a custom control changes how TestCases are built
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Expecting special TestSteps or a different workflow for a widget backed by a custom control.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: The Module/TestStep workflow can remain familiar, but supported control actions depend on the adapter. Inspect and test its capabilities rather than assuming every ActionMode works.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What does a custom control do?

options.text: It records a video of the widget for later comparison.
It wraps a complex UI widget so Tosca presents it as one of its standard UI elements, refining how Tosca detects that element.
It replaces the Engine used by the Module.
It converts the widget into an image-based control automatically.

practiceQuiz.hint: The goal is to make a non-standard widget look standard to Tosca.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The exercise’s DLLs enable the customized combo box and DIV table to be recognized and steered through appropriate Modules. Recognition and supported operations still depend on the extension, target and product version.

optionExplanations.A: Video capture is not the recognition adaptation described here.
optionExplanations.B: A compatible adapter can expose a complex widget through standard element recognition.
optionExplanations.C: An adapter does not by itself establish an automatic engine replacement.
optionExplanations.D: Structural adaptation is not an automatic conversion to image matching.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which sequence does the original Tosca 16.0 AE1 exercise prescribe before rescanning with its custom-control DLLs?

options.text: Export a TestCase, check it in, then rescan without deploying any DLL.
Rescan the original Module to compile the missing DLL automatically.
Close Tosca, copy the extracted lesson DLLs to the documented TBox directory, reopen Commander, then rescan.
Upload only to Tosca Cloud and assume the on-prem Commander installation changes automatically.

practiceQuiz.hint: The compiled extensions must be available to the on-prem installation before a fresh scan.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The original exercise explicitly uses the local TBox directory and a close/copy/reopen/rescan sequence. Its path is scoped to the training installation; Cloud upload is a different product workflow.

optionExplanations.A: Repository objects do not supply the exercise’s external DLLs.
optionExplanations.B: XScan consumes recognition behavior; the exercise installs compiled DLLs rather than generating them by rescanning.
optionExplanations.C: This is the original exercise’s deployment and activation sequence, using the documented training-installation path.
optionExplanations.D: Cloud distribution does not affect the on-prem customizations used in this exercise.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A test requires a custom DLL adapter, but the execution agent is missing that dependency. Which issue should the team address?

options.text: The Module needs to be rescanned on the agent.
Deploy the compatible adapter using its product-specific instructions; test object check-in alone does not provide the dependency.
Custom controls only work in Scratchbook, not in ExecutionLists.
The agent needs a different licence.

practiceQuiz.hint: Checking in test objects does not by itself deploy their external dependencies.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The scenario explicitly identifies the missing dependency. Verify its compatible deployment; this is not evidence that every real agent failure is caused by a missing DLL.

optionExplanations.A: Rescanning does not deploy the scenario’s missing external adapter.
optionExplanations.B: The specified missing dependency must be deployed and validated using the applicable instructions.
optionExplanations.C: The scenario identifies a missing DLL, not a Scratchbook-only limitation.
optionExplanations.D: No licensing diagnosis follows from the specified missing dependency.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What is a potential benefit of a compatible structural adapter over purely image-based identification?

options.text: Image-based controls are not supported on Windows applications.
It can reduce reliance on the widget’s pixel appearance, but its robustness still needs validation.
Image-based controls require a separate licence.
Custom controls execute the TestCase faster in every situation.

practiceQuiz.hint: Think about what each approach is actually matching on.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Structural recognition can reduce dependence on appearance. It does not guarantee that all layout, widget, styling or resolution changes are harmless.

optionExplanations.A: This is not the reason for a structural approach; visual identification can be evaluated for supported targets.
optionExplanations.B: Reducing dependence on pixel appearance is a potential benefit, subject to adapter validation.
optionExplanations.C: The cited source does not establish this blanket licensing distinction.
optionExplanations.D: No universal speed advantage is established by choosing an adapter.

quickRecap.value: Compatible DLL extensions enable the exercise combo box and DIV table to be scanned and steered as the corresponding controls.
Refines element detection; familiar test authoring may remain applicable, subject to supported actions.
AE1 Lesson 06 attachments: FancyComboBox.dll and HtmlTable.dll. Other widgets need their own applicable supported extension.
Tosca 16.0 exercise: close Tosca → copy extracted DLLs to its TBox directory → reopen Commander → rescan. Cloud upload does not deploy on-prem customizations.
Rescan and save the combo-box Module; use Planned with Input in the training TestCase and validate in ScratchBook. Also validate the DIV table.
Independent guidance: check supported identification, alternative engines, adapters and then visual approaches as applicable.
